reviewed-spanish-chicken-and-sweetcorn-s.name: Spanish Chicken and Sweetcorn Stew
ingredients: 1 x 400g (14oz) can of cannellini or haricot beans in water
steps: Rinse the beans, mash with a potato masher until none are left whole, and add to the slow cooker pot with the rest of the ingredients.
Half-fill the empty passata container with cold water, swilling out any left in the corners, and add that too.
Stir well, flattening out the chicken, then put the lid on and cook on HIGH for 3 hours or LOW for 5-6 hours until the chicken is very tender.
Serve as is, or with potatoes, pasta or rice, or soft flatbreads for dunking. Garnish with chopped herbs if you like.

reviewed-proper-beef-stew-and-dumplings.name: Proper Beef Stew and Dumplings
ingredients: For the dumplings: 200g (1⅓ cups) self-raising flour, plus extra for dusting
steps: Finely dice the celery, onion and carrots. Cook in a large frying pan with a little oil for about 5 minutes until starting to soften.
Meanwhile, coat the beef in the flour, shaking off the excess. Peel and quarter the potatoes.
Transfer the softened veg to the slow cooker. Brown the beef in batches in the same pan over high heat until dark and crispy outside but still raw inside, then transfer to the slow cooker too.

Add the potatoes and remaining ingredients (bay leaves, garlic, mixed herbs, Worcestershire sauce) plus a generous grind of black pepper. Mix the stock cubes with 800ml (3½ cups) boiling water until dissolved and add that too. Stir well.
Cook for 6-8 hours on LOW or 4-5 hours on HIGH, until the meat is tender and falls apart with gentle pressure.

Optional dumplings: 1 hour before serving, mix the dumpling ingredients with a pinch of black pepper and about 160ml (⅔ cup) cold water into a slightly sticky, mouldable dough. Roll into golf-ball-sized dumplings (makes about 10) and drop into the stew.
Cook uncovered on HIGH until the dumplings have doubled in size - don't lift the lid while they rise.

reviewed-lamb-tagine.name: Lamb Tagine
ingredients: 750g (1lb 10oz) lamb shoulder, diced, most excess fat removed
1 x 400g (14oz) can chickpeas in water, drained
2 low-salt chicken or beef stock cubes, crumbled
steps: Heat 1 tbsp of the sunflower oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Fry half the lamb in an even layer for 2 minutes until browned, turn and fry another 1-2 minutes, then transfer to the slow cooker. Repeat with the remaining lamb.
Meanwhile, grate or finely dice the onion, peel the carrots and cut into chunks. Add these to the slow cooker along with the rest of the ingredients.

Once all the meat is browned and in the slow cooker, add 400ml (1⅔ cups) boiling water to the empty hot frying pan and stir for 30 seconds to lift the caramelized bits, then pour that flavoured water into the slow cooker.
Stir well, put the lid on, and cook for 4 hours on HIGH or 6-7 hours on LOW until the meat is super tender.
Serve in bowls with boiled potatoes and fresh herbs to garnish.

reviewed-coconut-potato-curry.name: Coconut Potato Curry
steps: Peel and grate (or finely dice) the onion. Finely grate the garlic. Add both to the slow cooker with the oil and stir. Cook for 10-15 minutes on HIGH.
Meanwhile, peel the potatoes and dice into bite-sized (about 3cm/1¼in) chunks.
Add the tomato purée, garam masala and curry powder to the slow cooker and stir. Cook for a further 10 minutes.

Once aromatic and the onion has started to cook, add the coconut milk and potatoes. Fill the empty coconut milk can with boiling water, crumble in the stock cube, and add to the slow cooker. Stir, and cook for 3 hours on HIGH or 5 hours on LOW.
After that time, add the frozen spinach and cook for a further 30 minutes on HIGH or 1 hour on LOW.
Serve piled into bowls with a flatbread tucked into the side of each dish.

reviewed-chicken-kyiv-pasta.name: Chicken Kyiv Pasta
steps: Add the chicken thighs, grated courgette, garlic, a good grinding of black pepper, and the butter to the slow cooker pot.

Boil the kettle and dissolve the stock cube in 550ml (2½ cups) of water, then add this to the chicken too. Stir really well so the chicken is unravelled and submerged under the stock. Put the lid on and cook on HIGH for 3 hours, or LOW for 6 hours.

Once the chicken is soft and tender, in a separate bowl mix the cream cheese and milk until well combined, then pour into the slow cooker along with the uncooked pasta. Stir really well, slightly squashing each piece of chicken with the wooden spoon to help it break up.
Put the lid back on and cook for 40 minutes on HIGH or 1 hour on LOW. Once done, stir really well, then put the lid on to stand for 5 minutes before stirring again and serving.
For an even creamier, cheesier texture, stir in the grated Cheddar once everything is cooked, then let it stand for 5 minutes so it melts into the sauce.

reviewed-creamy-butternut-squash-pasta.name: Creamy Butternut Squash Pasta
ingredients: 1 large butternut squash, peeled, deseeded and roughly chopped (approx. 800g-1kg/1lb 12oz-2lb 4oz chopped weight)
1 low-salt chicken or vegetable stock cube
steps: Boil the kettle.

Add the chopped butternut squash, onion and garlic to the slow cooker with a generous grinding of black pepper. Crumble in the stock cube, then add 500ml (generous 2 cups) of boiling water. Stir to dissolve the stock cube, then put the lid on and cook for 3 hours on HIGH or 5-6 hours on LOW until the veg is very tender.
Blend the veg and cooking liquid to a very smooth purée (a stick blender or food processor both work), then pour it back into the slow cooker.

Add the uncooked pasta, milk, cream cheese, grated smoked cheese and smoked paprika to the purée and stir well. Put the lid back on and cook for a further 30-40 minutes on LOW, or until the pasta is cooked.

Serve as is - adults can add a touch of salt and pepper. Also great the next day as a pasta bake: pour into an oven dish with a splash more milk, top with extra cheese, and bake at 200°C fan (220°C/425°F/Gas 7) for around 20 minutes until crisp and golden.

reviewed-chickpea-and-butternut-squash-d.name: Chickpea and Butternut Squash Dahl
ingredients: 1 butternut squash, peeled and cut into 2cm (¾in) dice
1 x 400g (14oz) can of chickpeas in water
a good grinding of black pepper
steps: Put all of the ingredients, including the water from the can of chickpeas, into the slow cooker pot, along with 350ml (1½ cups) of boiling water.
Give it a really good stir and pop the lid on. Cook for 3-4 hours on HIGH or 6-8 hours on LOW.
Once done, use a wooden spoon or rubber spatula to give the dahl a really good stir and mash the soft butternut squash into the sauce a little.
Serve with rice or naan breads, or use as a pasta sauce. Adults may want to season their portion with a little salt or a dash of chilli sauce.
